objects.description: Doubly-linked intrusive list node used as both the list head (sentinel) and embedded node within container structures. Each node has next and prev pointers. A list head is initialized to point to itself; membership is managed by the provided inline helpers and macros in this header.

Forward declaration for a generic IPC command header type abstracting different IPC ABI major versions. Only an incomplete type is provided here; the full definition is supplied by an ABI-specific header (e.g., ipc3/header.h or ipc4/header.h). Details such as fields and size are unknown in this header.

Common header included at the start of many IPC payload structures (non-command). Contains the size in bytes of the full structure including any extended data beyond the fixed struct. Packed and 4-byte aligned.
Header present at the beginning of all IPC command messages. size is the total message size (including any extension data), and cmd encodes global and command types. Packed and 4-byte aligned.

Generic reply format for IPC commands. Starts with sof_ipc_cmd_hdr followed by a signed error code (negative on error). Some commands may extend this by adding fields after error. Packed and 4-byte aligned.

Header for compound IPC commands (SOF_IPC_GLB_COMPOUND). Contains a command header and a count of subsequent commands in the current block; a count of 0 indicates the end of the compound sequence. Packed and 4-byte aligned.
Architecture-specific header for DSP oops (crash) reports. Records architecture identifier and total size of the oops message. Packed and 4-byte aligned.

Platform-specific header for DSP oops (crash) reports. Captures platform configuration ID (split high/low), number of special registers reported, and stack pointer information. Packed and 4-byte aligned.
Enumeration of stream buffer formats used in IPC to describe whether audio samples are interleaved or non-interleaved in memory.
Enumeration of stream direction for IPC messages: playback (output) or capture (input).
Describes a host buffer shared with DSP for streaming, including physical base address, number of pages, and total size. Begins with a generic IPC header.

Full parameter block for configuring a stream: header, host buffer, direction, sample/frame format, buffer format, rate, channel configuration, period size, and optional extended data and channel map. Fields reference enums defined elsewhere (e.g., sof_ipc_frame).
IPC command structure to set PCM parameters for a component. Contains command header, component ID, PCM flags, and the embedded stream parameters block.
Reply structure for PCM params command, carrying reply header, component ID, and the offset to a position report area.
Generic IPC command structure for stream lifecycle actions (e.g., free). Contains command header and target component ID.

objects.definition:
struct sof_ipc_stream_posn {
	struct sof_ipc_reply rhdr;
	uint32_t comp_id;	/**< host component ID */
	uint32_t flags;		/**< SOF_TIME_ */
	uint32_t wallclock_hz;	/**< frequency of wallclock in Hz */
	uint32_t timestamp_ns;	/**< resolution of timestamp in ns */
	uint64_t host_posn;	/**< host DMA position in bytes */
	uint64_t dai_posn;	/**< DAI DMA position in bytes */
	uint64_t comp_posn;	/**< comp position in bytes */
	uint64_t wallclock;	/**< audio wall clock */
	uint64_t timestamp;	/**< system time stamp */
	uint32_t xrun_comp_id;	/**< comp ID of XRUN component */
	int32_t xrun_size;	/**< XRUN size in bytes */
} __attribute__((packed, aligned(4)));
objects.description: Position report message structure providing timestamp, wallclock, and byte positions for host and DAI DMA, plus XRUN information. Flags indicate validity, sync, and 32/64-bit sizing of timestamps.

Packed trace/log message header used to precede a variable-length array of uint32_t arguments. Contains a unique identifier, split bitfields for two IDs (e.g., pipeline and component), an 8-bit core identifier, a 64-bit timestamp in DSP ticks, and the originating log entry's ELF address. The bitfield layout depends on TRACE_ID_LENGTH (12). Consumers should treat instances as packed; beware of endianness and bitfield packing rules across compilers/ABIs.

functions.name: list_init
functions.description: Initializes a list head or standalone list_item so that it points to itself (empty list sentinel). Use this before any operations on a new list head or before reusing an item as a fresh, standalone list.
requirements: list must be a valid, writable pointer to struct list_item (non-NULL).
Must be called before using a list head for prepend/append/iteration.
After calling, list_is_empty(list) will be true.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if accessed concurrently.

functions.name: list_item_prepend
functions.signature: static inline void list_item_prepend(struct list_item *item, struct list_item *list)
functions.description: Inserts item at the beginning (head) of the doubly-linked intrusive list whose head is list. After insertion, item becomes the first element after the head.
requirements: item and list must be valid, writable pointers to struct list_item (non-NULL).
list must be an initialized list head (i.e., previously passed to list_init or LIST_INIT).
item must not be currently linked in any list (typically freshly initialized via list_init); otherwise list corruption may occur (inferred from intrusive list semantics).
item must not be the same address as list.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if accessed concurrently.

functions.name: list_item_append
functions.signature: static inline void list_item_append(struct list_item *item, struct list_item *list)
functions.description: Inserts item at the end (tail) of the doubly-linked intrusive list whose head is list. After insertion, item becomes the last element before the head.
requirements: item and list must be valid, writable pointers to struct list_item (non-NULL).
list must be an initialized list head (i.e., previously passed to list_init or LIST_INIT).
item must not be currently linked in any list (typically freshly initialized via list_init); otherwise list corruption may occur (inferred from intrusive list semantics).
item must not be the same address as list.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if accessed concurrently.

functions.name: list_item_del
functions.description: Removes item from whatever list it is currently linked into and reinitializes item to a self-referential empty list. After deletion, list_is_empty(item) will be true.
requirements: item must be a valid, writable pointer to struct list_item (non-NULL).
item must currently be linked into a well-formed list (its next and prev must be valid reciprocal neighbors).
After this call, item is no longer part of the original list and is reinitialized; do not continue to use any saved iterators pointing to the removed node.
Not thread-safe; external synchronization required if accessed concurrently.

functions.name: list_item_is_last
functions.signature: static inline int list_item_is_last(struct list_item *item, struct list_item *list)
functions.description: Returns nonzero if item is the last element in the list headed by list (i.e., if item->next == list). Intended for checks during traversal.
requirements: item and list must be valid pointers to struct list_item (non-NULL).
list must be the initialized head of the list being queried.
item should be a node currently linked in the same list as list; passing the head as item is not meaningful (inferred).
Result is 0 or nonzero integer; no errors are reported via return value.

functions.name: list_relink
functions.signature: static inline void list_relink(struct list_item *new_list, struct list_item *old_list)
functions.description: Repairs list links after the list head (sentinel) has moved to a new memory address. Updates neighbor nodes that still point to old_list so they point to new_list. If the list was empty, reinitializes the new head.
requirements: new_list and old_list must be valid pointers to struct list_item (non-NULL).
new_list must contain the moved/copy of the old head (its next/prev fields reflect the pre-move state); call this immediately after the head’s storage address changes.
old_list must be the previous address of the same list head; other nodes are unchanged.
Safe when the list is empty; in that case new_list is reinitialized to an empty head.
No concurrent modifications during relinking; external synchronization required.
